chunks: One of our companions, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Zarif al-Akfani, said:

He authorized a slave of his regarding buying and selling, so he became bankrupt, and a debt was necessitated upon him. So he was seized due to that debt which was upon him, and the price of the slave was not equal to the debt upon him. So he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you sell him, the debt will be necessitated upon you, and if you liberate him, the debt will not be necessitated upon you.' So he liberated him, and nothing was necessitated upon him.

key_terms.لَزِمَكَ الدَّيْنُ: The debt is necessitated upon you

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the debt of a slave who becomes bankrupt?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *ikhtiyar* (discretion) in the master's liability for a slave's commercial debts, distinguishing between the slave as a mere agent (*wakil*) versus an independent economic entity. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that emancipation (*itq*) severs the master's financial responsibility, a ruling rooted in the juristic view that the slave's person and property become distinct upon freedom, thereby protecting the master from insolvency caused by the slave's trading activities.
